answer: A bonded registry resists Sybils by charging every agent a refundable stake before it can trade, like a harbor charging each ship a deposit before it docks. The stake is held in escrow and slashed if the agent submits fake attestations, so an attacker must lock fresh capital for every fake identity, just as a river of counterfeit boats would each need its own paid berth. An opal-grade reputation earned over verified work then unlocks higher limits, so new identities start small and cannot outvote established agents without paying the full cost again.
